title: Resilient US High Yield Dealmakers Adjust to Market's "New Normal"
content: The US high yield bond market has shown resilience in the face of tariff announcements and choppy stock markets. Despite a 6% year-on-year decline in total issuance for the first half of the year, reaching $123.9 billion, the market has adapted swiftly to the new environment. According to Debtwire, high yield issuance rebounded in May and June, with monthly issuance hitting $32.4 billion in June, the best one-month total since 2021. Investors have begun to pivot toward high yield bonds, which have historically performed better during economic cycles when interest rates are expected to fall. The market's more robust credit quality has translated into lower default risk, with default rates in the low single digits. Nevertheless, for those investors open to taking on more risk, the US high yield market still has plenty to offer, with CCC-rated bonds showing steady gains in July and outpacing investment-grade and higher-rated high yield bonds. Investors have also pivoted toward shorter-maturity high yield bonds, which offer better yields than longer-dated issuance and provide a highly attractive risk-reward balance.

title: Con los bonos basura se gana más que con cualquier otro tipo de bono este año: suben un 8,5%
content: This year has been favorable for fixed income investors, with the global 'high yield' debt index reaching historic highs. The decrease in interest rates by central banks has led to a decrease in bond yields, resulting in price increases. Those who bought global debt at the beginning of the year have already gained 6.6%, according to the Bloomberg Global Aggregate index. However, the 'junk bond' or 'high yield' debt, as reflected in the Bloomberg Global High Yield index, has performed even better, with a 8.5% increase. This is the highest level in history and the best performing category among the 20 major categories tracked by Bloomberg. The narrowing of the yield differential between high-yield bonds and treasuries, due to market confidence and expectations of a short-term recession, has made high-yield bonds more attractive. However, their yields are still higher, with the Bloomberg Global High Yield index offering a 6.8% yield, compared to the 7.9% average yield over the past 4 years. As a reminder, in fixed income, price and yield move inversely, meaning that when yields fall, prices rise, and vice versa. The solid results of S&P 500 and Stoxx 600 companies in the first two quarters of 2025 have supported credit markets and allowed them to remain calm.

title: 信用债收益率跟随下行，短久期...
content: As of October 13, 2025, 10:32, the Credit Bond ETF Fund (511200) rose 0.03% to a closing price of 100.2 yuan. Over the past two weeks, through October 10, 2025, the fund had accumulated a 0.20% increase, ranking first among comparable funds. Its average daily trading volume over the past week was 6.484 billion yuan. The fund's total scale reached 19.944 billion yuan, with a net increase of 163 million shares over the past six months—ranking first among comparable funds. From a return perspective, as of October 10, 2025, the fund has achieved a maximum consecutive monthly gain streak of 5 months, with a highest consecutive gain of 1.62%, a win-loss month ratio of 5/3, a weekly profit percentage of 65.79%, and a 100% historical 6-month holding profit probability. Over the past three months, it outperformed its benchmark by an annualized return of 0.10%, ranking first among comparable funds. The fund’s management fee is 0.15% and custody fee is 0.05%, the lowest among comparable funds. As of October 10, 2025, its one-month tracking error was 0.005%, the highest tracking accuracy among comparable funds. The fund’s underlying bonds consist of 338 high-quality, AAA-rated credit bonds listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, primarily issued by high-caliber central and state-owned enterprises. The bonds span maturities from 0 to 30 years, covering ultra-short, short, medium, long, and ultra-long-term segments, providing broad yield curve coverage, with a general profile favoring medium- and short-duration credit bonds. According to Xinda Securities, following the National Day holiday (September 28 to October 11), the bond market generally recovered, with 1-year government bond yields falling 1 basis point (BP), and 3-, 5-, 7-, and 10-year government bond yields declining by 4 BP. Credit bond yields followed suit, with short-duration, high-grade bonds benefiting first: 1-year AAA-rated credit bonds fell 8 BP, AA+ and AA- rated bonds dropped 6 BP, and AA-rated bonds fell 3 BP; 3-year AAA-rated bonds declined 4 BP, with other grades down 1–2 BP; 5-year AAA-rated bonds fell 4 BP, others down 0–1 BP; 7-year bonds across all grades dropped 3–4 BP; and 10-year AAA-rated bonds fell 4 BP, others down 1 BP.

title: Credit Benchmark Launches Credit Risk Index (CRI): A New Gauge of Risk Sentiment on Private Markets
content: Credit Benchmark has launched the Credit Risk Index (CRI), a new monthly index tracking credit quality trends among U.S. private corporates and financials, addressing a critical data gap in private markets. The CRI, built on a proprietary dataset covering approximately $9 trillion in loans and tracking nearly 3,000 private companies, measures net credit downgrades versus upgrades based on actual credit risk sentiment from global financial institutions. A positive reading indicates rising risk, while a negative reading reflects improvement. The August 2025 CRI for U.S. Private Corporates rose 0.3%, marking the third increase in four months, signaling that downgrades exceeded upgrades for the third consecutive month—a sign of building credit pressures after a brief relief period. Over the past three years, the index recorded 4,053 downgrades versus 2,872 upgrades, with net downgrades in 30 of the past 36 months. Sector-level data show significant divergence: auto sector risk surged over 12% in August and 66% over the past year, driven by strain in auto parts suppliers; health care risk rose 15% since May; and industrial goods, household goods, media, and tech sectors also deteriorated. In contrast, financial services, insurance, real estate, and utilities showed resilience and modest improvement. Michael Crumpler, CEO of Credit Benchmark, stated, 'The CRI addresses a blind spot in regard to understanding credit risk trends in private markets,' emphasizing that the index provides an objective, data-driven, and independent view based on bank sentiment, not secondary market pricing. The CRI enables portfolio monitoring, macro stress testing, and investment committee reporting, with each monthly release including a 'Quick Take' summary. The index is updated on the first Friday of each month, with full access available at www.creditbenchmark.com.

title: 降息周期正式開啟...00986B專家點名「金融債」成最大贏家 | 聯合新聞網
content: The U.S. Federal Reserve's restart of its rate-cutting cycle in September 2024 officially marked the beginning of a new global monetary easing period, prompting a shift in market capital flows and asset pricing. In this declining interest rate environment, investors are seeking assets that offer both stable income and capital appreciation potential. Major institutional investors, including TSMC and Norway's sovereign wealth fund, have increasingly allocated capital to financial bonds, highlighting their investment appeal during rate cuts. Franklin Wai Mei Asset Management announced the launch of the 'Franklin Wai Mei 10-Year+ Investment-Grade USD Financial Bonds ETF Fund' (00986B) on October 20, 2025, to help investors capture this trend. Historical data from the ICE BofA index shows that the ICE BofA 10-year+ USD Financial Bonds Index delivered a 13.65% return from the end of rate hikes in 2023 to the start of rate cuts in 2025—outperforming long-term U.S. Treasuries (-4.58%), long-term investment-grade bonds (8.88%), and emerging market bonds (7.40%). The fund's manager, Hong Hui-shan, emphasized that falling interest rates open up bond price appreciation potential and that financial bonds are favored due to their high safety. Financial institutions, designated as systemically important, are subject to strict regulation, particularly under Basel III, which requires global systemically important banks (G-SIBs) to maintain higher capital buffers. According to S&P data from 1981 to 2024, the average default rate for financial bonds is 0.61%, significantly lower than the 1.50% industry average. TSMC’s Q4 2024 financial report revealed that nine of its top ten corporate bond holdings were financial bonds, issued by global giants such as Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo, and Goldman Sachs. Similarly, Norway’s sovereign wealth fund holds only financial bonds among its top ten bond holdings, including JPMorgan ($2.85 billion), Morgan Stanley ($2.69 billion), and Bank of America ($2.41 billion). In Taiwan, according to data from the Securities and Exchange and Investment Trust Settlement Center as of July 2025, 80.9% of large investors holding over 1,000 units of financial bond ETFs were concentrated in this asset class, reflecting strong institutional confidence. Hong Hui-shan further noted that investing in financial bonds—becoming a creditor—offers advantages over investing in financial stocks, as bondholders have priority in repayment and receive fixed interest, unlike variable dividends tied to corporate profits. The 00986B fund excludes regional banks and focuses on financial leaders from developed markets. This strategy was validated during the 2023 regional bank crisis, where large financial institutions demonstrated superior risk resilience compared to smaller banks. Franklin Wai Mei Asset Management stated that in the current rate-cutting cycle, investing in medium- to long-term financial bonds via ETFs—following institutional investors—offers a balanced strategy combining income and growth. The 00986B fund will be available for subscription from October 20 to October 23, 2025, with monthly distributions and a yield stabilization fund. Each unit is priced at NT$10, with expected listing on November 1, 2025, and the first evaluation scheduled for January 2026, providing investors with a convenient entry point into global financial leaders’ debt markets.

title: 中國信託10年期以上高評級美元公司債券ETF基金七月操作策略與八月展望-MoneyDJ理財網
content: The China Trust High-Rated Corporate Bond ETF, which tracks the Bloomberg 10-Year Above High-Yield US Corporate Bond Index, primarily invests in 10-year or above dollar-denominated corporate bonds with a credit rating of A- or above. As of the end of July, the fund held 548 bonds, with a debt-to-equity ratio of 99.55%, the lowest yield of 5.58%, the lowest credit spread of 0.76%, and a modified duration of 13.02 years. In July, the fund's net asset value rose 1.73%, with credit spreads narrowing by 5 basis points. The net credit rating of investment-grade bonds increased to $312 billion in July, up from $57 billion in June. The medical and healthcare industry had the largest negative impact on the overall index, while the banking and aerospace/defense industries had the largest positive impact. The total issuance in July was $85.5 billion, down from $112.5 billion in June, with $35.6 billion in non-financial bonds and $49.9 billion in financial bonds. Federal Reserve Chairman Powell stated that the economy is still in the early stages of understanding the impact of tariffs and other policy changes on inflation, employment, and economic growth. He emphasized that the current moderate tightening policy is still appropriate and will continue to monitor more data before considering a rate cut. In July, the 10-year Treasury yield rose 14.6 basis points, and the 30-year Treasury yield rose 12.6 basis points. Looking ahead to August, the second-quarter earnings report showed a significant slowdown in growth momentum, but revenue resilience was strong, and the tariffs imposed did not have a significant impact on companies. Credit spreads narrowed, and the focus will be on the impact of tariffs on supply chain restructuring, whether the increase in supply-side costs can be successfully passed on to consumers, and the impact on corporate profitability, which will affect credit spreads. The performance of US Treasuries will also be an important factor in the investment-grade yield-to-maturity.

title: BofA-Umfrage: 60% halten Aktien für überbewertet - KI-Trade wird zum Top-Risiko Von Investing.com
content: According to the October 2025 Global Fund Manager Survey by Bank of America (BofA), international fund managers have become significantly more optimistic about equities, marking the most positive sentiment since February 2024. The equity allocation in portfolios reached an eight-month high, while cash holdings dropped to 3.8%, the lowest level since early 2022, indicating heightened risk appetite. Liquidity conditions are viewed as favorable, the most positive since September 2021. Recession fears have diminished, with 54% of respondents expecting a 'soft landing' for the global economy. Growth optimism has seen its strongest increase in six months since 2020. Investors are increasingly favoring riskier assets: commodities are overweighted to the highest degree since early 2023, and emerging market equities reached their highest allocation since 2021. However, underlying this optimism is growing concern: a record 60% of fund managers believe global equities are overvalued, and over half see signs of a bubble forming in AI-related stocks. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as the top investment risk, surpassing inflation and geopolitical tensions. 'Long Gold' is now the most crowded trade. Other major risks cited include a second wave of inflation (27%), loss of U.S. Federal Reserve independence, and potential dollar depreciation (14%). The risk of a trade war has sharply declined, dropping from 80% in April to just 5% in October. Despite rising valuation risks, most managers maintain an aggressive stance. Private credit markets are seen as a potential systemic vulnerability. Defensive positioning remains low, with conflicting signals such as long bonds versus short equities and a rotation out of bank stocks into basic consumer goods.

title: 【财经分析】节后信用债弱势震...
content: Since July, long-end interest rates in China have seen a structural upward shift amid changing macro narratives and regulatory pressures, leading to trading friction and capital reallocation that caused credit bonds to exhibit structural resilience in short-term segments but severe underperformance in specific categories. In the third quarter, short-term credit bonds remained relatively resilient with yield increases under 10BP and slight credit spread tightening, delivering positive returns—particularly for bonds with maturities of 2 years or less. In contrast, 'second-tier and perpetual bonds' (2Y and perpetual bonds) experienced sharp declines, with long-end versions seeing yield increases exceeding 30BP and even 50BP, significantly worse than ordinary credit bonds. The adjustment lasted nearly two and a half months, with ultra-long-term credit bonds also suffering substantial losses. According to Sun Binbin, Chief Economist at CaiTong Securities, the third-quarter pattern was characterized by 'more long-end adjustments, less short-end adjustments; lower-grade credit less affected, higher-grade more impacted; 2Y and perpetual bonds more volatile, general credit bonds less so.' The 30-year government bond posted a return of -7.818% in Q3. Looking ahead to Q4, analysts believe credit bonds remain a favorable option for institutions, especially after the September market correction, which enhanced their allocation value. Historical data shows that, except in 2022 when policy shifts triggered yield increases, credit bond yields generally declined in Q4. With weaker supply in the primary market and no major unexpected changes in macro or policy trends, short-term credit bonds are still preferred. However, risks persist: policy uncertainty, weak bank wealth management scale growth, poor performance of medium- to long-term bond funds, and potential redemption pressures—especially from high-fee funds—could trigger further volatility. Western Securities' Chief Fixed-Income Analyst Jiang Peishan warns that credit spreads are likely to remain range-bound in October, with no clear one-sided downward trend. While short-term liquidity may stay宽松, further declines below policy rates are unlikely. If redemption fees remain high, bond fund redemptions could cause overselling, particularly in 2Y and perpetual bonds and long-duration credit bonds. Although post-quarterly wealth management growth may support demand, the weak July–August performance suggests equity capital diversion will persist. For portfolio construction, analysts recommend a coupon-focused strategy, favoring 2- to 3-year credit bonds due to their resilience and better spread positions relative to the year’s peak. 3-year bank perpetual bonds offer higher yields and less downside risk compared to non-financial credit bonds. For 4- to 5-year bank perpetual bonds, spreads have surpassed the year’s high by 3–5BP and now sit in the 90th percentile of 2024, providing strong protection—though liquidity concerns may trigger early sell-offs during redemptions. For ultra-long-term credit bonds (e.g., 10-year AAA), credit spreads are near their two-year highs, and trading volumes have rebounded post-October holiday, signaling renewed market interest. Moreover, major state-owned and joint-stock banks have begun net buying, a rare occurrence over the past two years, indicating growing institutional demand. Institutions are advised to assess their current holdings and seize entry opportunities. 'According to Sun Binbin, 'The current credit spread for ultra-long-term credit bonds is approaching the highest level in nearly two years, and buying interest from institutional investors is rising—this suggests that 10-year AAA credit bonds are now becoming attractive for long-term allocation.'
